topic: Single-leg strength: why Pilates trains one side at a time

slides.headline: Is one leg doing all the work?
slides.sub: Why Pilates often trains one side at a time.

slides.title: Most of life is single-leg
slides.body: Walking, stairs, running, stepping out of a car: you're mostly on one leg at a time. Training both legs together is useful, but it can hide a side that's quietly doing less.

slides.title: Two-leg moves can hide a gap
slides.body: In a squat or leg press, the stronger side often takes a bit more load without you noticing. Working one side at a time shows the difference and gives the quieter side its fair share.

slides.title: Balance comes along for the ride
slides.body: Standing on one leg asks your hip, knee and foot to work as a team. Single-leg footwork on the reformer builds strength and steadiness together, at a load you can control.

slides.title: Try this at home
slides.body: Single-leg sit-to-stand from a high chair, 6 to 8 per side, holding a bench if needed. Lower the chair or slow the movement as it gets easier. Note which side feels harder.

slides.title: Uneven isn't always a problem
slides.body: Small differences between sides are normal. If one leg is clearly weaker after an injury, or a knee, hip or ankle hurts during single-leg work, it's worth an assessment first.

slides.headline: Want both legs pulling their weight?
slides.body: Our Pilates team checks how each side moves, then builds a program with the right single-leg work for you. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
Is one leg quietly doing more than its share?

Most of what we do, from walking and stairs to running for the train, happens on one leg at a time. Two-leg exercises are useful, but the stronger side can take over without you noticing.

That's why clinical Pilates often works one side at a time. Single-leg footwork on the reformer, split stances and step-ups show up the difference between sides and build strength and balance together, at a load you can control.

Small differences are normal. A clearly weaker leg after an injury, or pain during single-leg work, is worth an assessment before you push on.

With uni and school back and winter sport preseason starting, it's a good time to even things up. Book online via the link in bio.
